placements.theme: An instrument's operational trust is established through documented, reference-checked calibration, not by default.

placements.title: A calibration only counts once it is checked against a known standard across the full range it will be used in
placements.theme: Trust in an instrument's calibration comes from verifying it against an independent reference across its full operating band, not from setting the value alone.
placements.why: src-1 and src-2 are Quill's direct testimony that the Kestrelwood spectrograph is calibrated at 88.4 MHz and that this was verified against the June reference plates across the full observing band; src-4 is the record's condensed restatement of the same finding with Quill as principal. Together these are the position's core finding, but per the narrative grain test a specific frequency/date/instrument is a fact, not a theme — it evidences a recurring, future-feedable subject about calibration practice (setting a value AND independently verifying it) rather than being that subject itself. No existing leaf or strata (both empty) plausibly held this, and nothing supplied was even close enough to warrant lineage, so this is a standalone NEW mint under the freshly minted Calibration stratum.
